title: Partial sums and kernel projections for supplied quotient presentations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M\in\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{v}(R)$, and $E$ a linearly ordered type with well-founded strict order, with no universe relation imposed. Let $F_e\subseteq M$ be monotone and exhaustive and let $P(e)$ be supplied projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] of $F_e/(\sup_{i<e}F_i\cap F_e)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. There exist a short exact complex $S$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] with $S_3=M$ and categorically projective $S_2$, and monotone exhaustive submodules $H_e\subseteq S_2$. Put $K_e=S_1\cap H_e$, precisely the inverse image along $S.f$, and $V_e=(\sup_{i<e}K_i)\cap K_e$ viewed as a submodule of $K_e$. For every $e$, either $V_e=K_e$ or there is a surjective $R$-linear map $q_e:K_e\to\ker(P(e)_0\to Q_e)$ whose linear kernel is exactly $V_e$. These maps come from component projections in the active-index direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], not from an asserted quotient isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension), successor proof: projective presentation, kernel intersections, and exact sequence of successive quotients

proof.text: For each nonzero Q_e lift the given augmentation P(e)_0 → Q_e across F_e → Q_e by categorical projectivity. Use zero summands for zero Q_e. Define the map from the external direct sum B to M as the finite sum of those lifts and stage inclusions. Induction on e shows the partial sum through e surjects onto F_e: subtract a lift of the quotient class and lift the remainder from the predecessor union. The predecessor supremum is the union of its directed nonempty chain; at a least stage it is zero.

For each active index choose an element of F_e outside U_e. Such elements at different indices differ: the element at the smaller index is in the predecessor supremum at the larger index. Thus active indices inject into M and are small in universe v. Shrink these indices and form the direct sum B of their degree-zero projectives in universe v. A map out of B lifts across any epimorphism by choosing lifts on the individual projective summands and summing them; this verifies categorical projectivity directly, without converting it to unrestricted module projectivity.

Use S as the kernel complex of the constructed surjection, with H_e the partial direct sum through e in the middle object. These H_e are monotone and exhaustive by finite support; an index for empty support exists by hcover at zero. Pullback along S.f gives K_e.

At each active e, restrict the component projection to K_e and transport its linear augmentation-kernel codomain to the categorical kernel. Lift the image of any augmentation-kernel vector from the predecessor partial sum and subtract it to prove surjectivity. The projection kernel is the predecessor supremum of K_i by finite support. At an inactive e no summand is added, so that predecessor submodule is top. Stop before taking the quotient isomorphism.

theorem exists_projective_presentation_kernel_projection_data
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E] [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)]
    (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
    (P : ∀ e : E, ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
        ((⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, F i.val).comap (F e).subtype)))) :
    ∃ S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R), S.X₃ = M ∧ S.ShortExact ∧
      Projective S.X₂ ∧ ∃ H : E → Submodule R S.X₂,
        Monotone H ∧ (∀ x : S.X₂, ∃ e : E, x ∈ H e) ∧
        ∀ e : E,
          let K : E → Submodule R S.X₁ := fun i ↦ (H i).comap S.f.hom
          let U := (⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, K i.val).comap (K e).subtype
          U = ⊤ ∨ ∃ q : K e →ₗ[R] (kernel ((P e).π.f 0) : ModuleCat.{v} R),
            Function.Surjective q ∧ q.ker = U
